architect.rationale: single-loop: five ordered commits on one branch of the orchestra git repo (main @ 7e62e10). Not a diamond, because no three slices have disjoint file sets. session/mod.rs is the hub: s2 adds stop_and_wait and the Fake wait, s3 adds the task map, the cwd resolver and the queue pump, s4 adds land, discard and cleanup. lib.rs is touched by s1 (mod git), s3 (worktree base, task-updated event, commands) and s4 (commands). commands.rs is touched by s3 and s4, and git.rs by s1 (runner, worktree add/remove) and s4 (diff, commit, merge). Only the frontend (s5) is file-disjoint from the backend, and it consumes the IPC shapes of s3 and s4, so it is a sequence, not a parallel branch. Order: s1 first (the s2 removal probe and the s3 worktree add call git.rs), s2 before s3 (s3 suspends a done task child through stop_and_wait), s3 before s4 (land operates on the Task entity), s5 last. Risk: every slice is high. s1 runs a new external program against the user repositories. s2 changes kill/exit semantics beside the locks and is the only evidence for the Windows removal race. s3 changes the on-disk schema and where claude runs. s4 writes the user project checkout and deletes directories. s5 renders untrusted diff text from the user project. Independently of those reasons, s1-s4 all share mod.rs, lib.rs or git.rs, which is high under the fleet rule. One flagged discrepancy that does not block the plan: the scout cites SessionList.tsx:148-195 and SessionDetail.tsx:217-264, but on disk those files are 75 and 195 lines (CRLF, counted with grep -c). The frontend line references are unreliable; the backend references checked here (mod.rs 374-436, 541-597, 643-653; store.rs 18-44, 89-92; process.rs 139-160) match.

design.task_session_relation: Task is its own entity in session/task.rs, kept in Inner.tasks next to Inner.sessions. The relation is one task to at most one session: task.session_id is None while queued, and session.task_id: Option<String> is set for a task session (None for a plain session, which is unchanged). A follow-up to a task reuses the same session through the existing reply and D2 lazy resume, so a task never gets a second session. Task status is a closed enum, separate from SessionStatus: queued, running, needs_input, done, landing, landed, discarded, cleanup_pending, error. running and needs_input are derived from the task session (Starting/Working -> running; WaitingPermission/WaitingQuestion/NeedsAttention -> needs_input). done is entered when the task session reaches Idle (Finished or Error item, with last_turn_error kept as a flag), Ended or Failed (with session_over: true, so no follow-up). The others are set explicitly. Why: Idle means turn over and can reply, and must not be conflated with done.
design.cwd: A session working dir comes from one resolver, Inner::cwd_of(session) -> Result<PathBuf, CwdError>: the project path for a plain session, and task.worktree for a task session. start, resume_with and the queue pump all call it, and none of them reads projects.get(project_id).path directly any more. Before every spawn it checks is_dir and returns a fixed message (task worktree, or project folder, no longer exists) without spawning. Restore never spawns (D2 rule kept). It checks each task worktree with is_dir and puts a missing one into error with note worktree missing. The cwd of a task session is fixed for life, so resume always runs in the directory the conversation started in. That sidesteps the scout unknown on whether claude keys resume by cwd. Resume after the worktree is gone is refused, never attempted elsewhere.
design.schema: SCHEMA becomes 2. load accepts 1 and 2 and refuses anything else (UnknownSchema, so the D2/D3 banner shows and nothing is saved). Snapshot gains next_task: u64 and tasks: Vec<StoredTask>, both serde(default). StoredSession gains task_id: Option<String>, serde(default). A schema-1 file therefore loads with no tasks and every session plain. The first save writes schema 2, and that one-way step is what the bump buys. A D3 build that meets a schema-2 file hits store.rs:89-92, shows the newer-version banner and saves nothing, instead of silently dropping the tasks on its next save. Stored task fields are strings parsed through the closed enums on load, and an unknown value loads as error with note unknown status rather than making the whole file Unreadable.
design.exit_wait_and_cleanup: Proc gains wait_exit(&self, timeout: Duration) -> bool. ProcessHandle keeps an Arc<(Mutex<bool>, Condvar)> that the reader thread sets after wait()/try_wait returns and before sink(Output::Exit). On Windows with a job, wait_exit also polls JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation.ActiveProcesses until 0 (or the timeout), so a grandchild still in the job keeps the wait open (the windows-sys JobObjects feature is already enabled). Sessions::stop_and_wait(session_id, timeout) does stop() and then waits with no lock held, returning Ok(true) once exited or Ok(false) on timeout. Cleanup (land or discard): stop_and_wait(10 s), then git worktree remove --force <path> with up to 5 attempts at 250/500/1000/2000/2000 ms, then git worktree prune. On success the branch is deleted (git branch -d after a land, -D after a discard). If anything still fails, the task goes to cleanup_pending with a short note: it is persisted, offers a Retry cleanup command, and is retried once by a background thread after restore, when no child can be alive. Paths are never removed with std::fs::remove_dir_all, and every path handed to git worktree remove must pass a containment check: canonicalised, it starts with the canonicalised app_data_dir/worktrees. That way a tampered state.json cannot direct a deletion.
design.git_invocation: New src-tauri/src/git.rs copies the process.rs shape. The program is the const GIT = git, resolved on PATH by std (no shell, no .cmd). Fixed leading args: -c core.longpaths=true -c core.quotepath=false --no-pager -C <repo PathBuf>. Fixed env: GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, plus GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 for status. CREATE_NO_WINDOW is set, stdin is null, and stdout is read with a byte cap. Every call has a timeout (30 s by default, 120 s for commit and merge), after which the child is killed. Typed inputs only: RepoPath (a Rust-held PathBuf), TaskBranch (a newtype matching ^orchestra/t[0-9]+(-[2-9])?$, built only by Rust), BaseBranch (read from git symbolic-ref --short HEAD, then checked with git check-ref-format --branch and must not start with -), and CommitId (40 or 64 lowercase hex). --end-of-options goes before ref operands wherever the subcommand accepts it. git::check() runs git --version, and a NotFound maps to a fixed message (Git was not found on PATH; tasks need Git for Windows). The check runs at task creation. Plain sessions never need git. Errors are short and fixed, and never echo git stderr or a path.
design.spawn_error_fix: process::spawn checks dir.is_dir() before Command::spawn and returns a fixed message (the working folder no longer exists). Only a NotFound with an existing dir keeps the claude.exe-not-on-PATH message.
design.project_requirements: To accept a task, a project must be a git work tree whose toplevel (git rev-parse --show-toplevel, canonicalised) equals the canonicalised project path, must have a HEAD commit, and must have HEAD on a branch (not detached). Otherwise create_task refuses with a fixed message and nothing is queued. Plain sessions in non-git folders keep working.
design.d5_note: D5 builders will create tasks through the same internal Sessions::create_task API that IPC uses. Task carries no fleet-specific field. The inbox stays per session, so the permission and question items of a task keep appearing there unchanged. Nothing for D5 is built here.

plan.intent: Task entity, schema 2, queue, and worktree cwd. New session/task.rs: Task, TaskStatus, StoredTask and pure transition functions. Sessions::create_task(project_id, prompt, settings) runs git::check, checks the project (design.project_requirements), records base_branch and base_commit, and inserts a queued task with id t<N> from a persisted next_task. Queue pump: while fewer than MAX_RUNNING_TASKS (gate G7) tasks are running or needs_input, the oldest queued task starts. The pump derives worktree = <worktree_base>/<project_id>/<task_id> and branch = orchestra/<task_id> (gate G6 collision suffix), runs git::worktree_add, then starts a session whose cwd comes from cwd_of. If the worktree cannot be created, the task goes to error with a fixed note and the pump moves on. The pump runs after create_task, after any task leaves running or needs_input, after cancel, and once after restore (gate G8; restore itself still spawns nothing). Task status follows its session through on_output, per design.task_session_relation. On entering done (gate G11) the child is suspended (state.suspend, then stop_and_wait off the reader thread), so the worktree has no live cwd and the slot frees. cancel_task applies to queued only (no worktree yet, nothing to clean). Plain sessions are untouched and never count toward the limit. Schema 2 as in design.schema. Sessions::with_writer takes the worktree base (app_data_dir/worktrees; a temp dir in tests). G1_land_target.recommended: base_branch recorded at task creation (the branch checked out in the project at that time). Land requires the checkout to still be on that branch and refuses otherwise.
alternatives: whatever branch the checkout is on at land time (simpler, but a task based on main can land on a feature branch)
never write the checkout: land = commit in the worktree, remove the worktree, keep orchestra/<id> for the owner to merge by hand

G2_dirty_checkout.recommended: refuse land when tracked files are modified or staged (status --porcelain --untracked-files=no non-empty); git itself refuses if an untracked file would be overwritten
alternatives: also refuse on any untracked file (stricter, annoying with build output)
auto-stash and pop (rejected in not_doing: a hidden change to the working tree of the owner)

G3_merge_method.recommended: git merge --no-ff --no-edit with message merge orchestra task <id>: <title>. One merge commit, task commits preserved, revertable with -m 1, and branch -d afterwards
alternatives: squash (merge --squash then one commit on base: linear history, task commits lost, branch -D)
--ff-only (refuses whenever base moved since task creation)

G4_land_confirm.recommended: an explicit in-app confirm naming the project, target branch, file count and method; Rust enforces the state and checkout checks regardless

G5_worktree_location.recommended: app_data_dir/worktrees/<project_id>/<task_id>: Rust-derived, inside the app base dir (the CLAUDE.md base-dir rule), never written beside the projects of the owner, containment-checked before any removal
alternatives: sibling of the project: <project parent>/.orchestra-worktrees/<project name>-<task_id> (shorter paths; for umbrella apps it sits under repos/, so the umbrella CLAUDE.md and .claude hooks still load; but it writes outside both the app data dir and the repo)
inside the repo: <project>/.orchestra/worktrees/<task_id> (needs a .gitignore entry in the repo of the owner; rejected)
G5_worktree_location.caveat: OWNER DECISION. With the recommended location, a task on an umbrella app runs claude outside repos/, so repos/CLAUDE.md and the repos/.claude commit-trailer guard do NOT load for it; only the CLAUDE.md of the app itself, inside the worktree, loads. Commits claude makes in such a worktree could carry attribution trailers. s5 shows every commit with its full message before land, so a trailer is visible at review, and the land and merge commits that Orchestra makes never add one. Also: every task writes the .git of the project (worktree metadata and the orchestra/<id> branch) from task start, not only at land.

G6_branch_naming.recommended: orchestra/<task_id> (t<N>, N persisted); on collision with an existing branch try -2 to -9, then refuse with a fixed message
alternatives: orchestra/<task_id>-<slug>, slug of [a-z0-9-] up to 32 chars from the title (more readable, more validation surface)

G7_concurrency.recommended: MAX_RUNNING_TASKS = 2, a Rust constant counting tasks in running or needs_input; plain sessions not counted
alternatives: configurable in the UI (deferred, see not_doing)

G8_queue_on_launch.recommended: lib.rs calls the pump once after restore, so queued tasks start on launch; restore itself never spawns. Tasks that were running or needs_input at close return as needs_input with the note paused when Orchestra closed, reply to continue, and do not count toward the limit until replied to

alternatives: same with --no-verify (skips the hooks of the owner; avoids a hook that hangs with no window)
refuse land while the worktree has uncommitted changes (the owner asks claude to commit first)

findings.issue: worktree_remove runs `git worktree remove --force <path>`, which on Git for Windows recurses through directory junctions (untracked) inside the worktree and deletes the files of the target. run() inherits GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE / GIT_INDEX_FILE from the parent environment; if set (e.g. cargo test run from a git hook, or the app launched from one), they override -C and git acts on the wrong repo/index. Consider env_remove on these.

Timeout kills only git.exe, not hooks or filter processes it spawned (post-checkout hook, git-lfs smudge during worktree add). A grandchild holding the stdout pipe also makes a successful call return Timeout after recv_timeout. Acceptable for s1; worth a job object if hooks prove common.

BaseBranch::parse is pub and accepts '@{-1}' and '@' (check-ref-format --branch resolves @{-N} and exits 0). Harmless today because its only input is symbolic-ref output and the value is only compared as a string, but the type does not guarantee a literal branch name.
symbolic-ref --short HEAD returns 'heads/main' when a tag 'main' also exists. s4 compares it with the same command's output, so consistent; any later use as a ref name would be wrong.
design.git_invocation says --end-of-options before ref operands; worktree add omits it. Operands are validated (absolute path, TaskBranch, hex CommitId) so not exploitable.

s2.summary: REJECT on one concrete flake; the production code is right. I reran all six done_when gates at tip 1e05204 in a detached worktree: all pass, and the full suite is 172 passed, 0 failed. Then I re-derived the ordering: the reader sets the latch and calls notify_all BEFORE sink(Output::Exit), which is the design. But wait_exit_returns_true_after_kill asserts rx.try_iter().last() is Exit straight after wait_exit returns, so the test races the reader thread. Over 190 repeat runs of the lib test binary it failed 3 times, with 'Exit was sent before wait_exit returned' at process.rs:317. The fix is to wait for Exit with rx.recv_timeout, or drop the assertion. Checked and OK: the condvar loop has no missed wakeup and honours the deadline. stop_and_wait holds no Inner while waiting. The reader never needs the latch lock to make progress, so there is no deadlock with on_output. The missing-dir check runs before spawn. stop, resume and shutdown are unchanged. Author is njcurtis3, no trailer, and the diff stays in the 3 s2 files.

findings.issue: wait_exit_returns_true_after_kill is flaky, and it is a done_when gate. The latch is set (process.rs ~251) before sink(Output::Exit) (~256), as design.exit_wait_and_cleanup specifies. So wait_exit can return true before the reader thread has sent Exit, and the non-blocking rx.try_iter().last() then sees no Exit. Measured: 1/150 failures running the test alone, and 2/40 with --test-threads=8 next to wait_exit_times_out_on_live_child. Panic: 'Exit was sent before wait_exit returned'. Fix: assert with rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5)) and drain to the Exit, or remove the assertion. Do not reorder latch and sink in production code: the design wants the latch first, so a waiter does not depend on on_output.

stop_and_wait re-reads s.proc after stop() released Inner. If a resume swaps in a new proc in that gap, it waits on the new live child and returns Ok(false) after the timeout. That is safe (cleanup goes to cleanup_pending) but avoidable: have stop return the proc it killed, or clone it under the same lock.

Job::active returns 0 when QueryInformationJobObject fails, so wait_exit reports true without having checked the grandchildren. That only happens with an invalid handle, so it is practically unreachable, but it is fail-open where everything else in wait_exit fails closed.

design.spawn_error_fix says to keep the claude.exe message only for 'a NotFound with an existing dir'. The dir is checked once, before spawn. If it vanishes between the check and CreateProcess, the claude.exe message comes back. This is a TOCTOU window of microseconds, acceptable as is. Re-checking dir.is_dir() inside the NotFound arm would close it.

removal_blocked_until_child_exits asserts retry.is_err(). That pins the git behaviour measured on this machine (the first blocked remove already unregistered the worktree), not something orchestra guarantees. It is honest, documented and recorded in the log, but a git version that keeps the registration on a failed delete would fail this probe even though cleanup is correct. Consider recording the retry result instead of asserting it.

stop_and_wait still re-reads s.proc after stop() released Inner (line now ~1468, not 659). A resume in that gap makes it wait on the new live child and return Ok(false) after timeout, which land_task/run_cleanup treat as 'still running' / cleanup_pending, so it fails safe. Having stop return the killed proc would remove the gap.

The recv_timeout loop sits after wait_exit(10 s), so its 5 s budget only covers reader-thread latency after the latch, which is microseconds. It is well bounded, and a hang cannot happen because the deadline is recomputed each pass.

The claude of any task can make a junction with no privilege. is_within only checks the worktree path itself. After a dirty-checkout refusal the task is Done with session_over=true and reply fails with "session is not running". findings.issue: Cleanup destroys data outside the worktree base through a junction. remove_worktree hands the worktree to git worktree remove --force, which on Windows recurses through NTFS junctions and deletes the target contents. I measured it with git 2.51.0.windows.1: a junction <wt>/link pointing at a canary dir with keep.txt and sub/deep.txt gave remove rc=0 and left the canary empty. I reproduced it end to end with a probe test: done_task, mklink /J <wt>/node_modules <canary outside base>, then discard_task returned Discarded and canary/keep.txt was gone. Land (run_cleanup Landed) and retry_cleanup take the same path. A task claude session can create a junction without privilege (for example a node_modules link into the owner project, the same pattern that emptied orchestra/desktop/node_modules today). is_within only checks the worktree path, never what is inside it. The containment rule and the no-remove_dir_all rule in the design both miss that the removal git itself does follows links. Fix: before the first git worktree remove, walk the worktree without following links (symlink_metadata / FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT). Remove each reparse point as a link only (fs::remove_dir on a junction, remove_file on a file symlink), or refuse to cleanup_pending with a fixed note. Add a test with a canary outside the base. Symlinks (mklink /D) need privilege on this machine and were not measured, but they need the same handling.

A refused land permanently ends the task conversation. land_task calls stop_and_wait(sid) before any check. stop() calls mark_stopped, which turns a Suspended session into Ended, and sync_task then sets task.session_over=true. Every later refusal (dirty checkout, branch moved, attribution, a hook refusing the leftover commit, nothing to land, conflict) leaves the task Done but with no follow-up. Probe: done_task, owner edits a.txt, land_task returns Err(uncommitted changes), then list_tasks shows session_over=true and reply(sid, please fix it) returns Err(session is not running). That contradicts the intent (refuse, nothing changed, the task stays done) and the G11 follow-up path. It also removes the natural remedy for the trailer refusal (ask claude to reword its commit) and for a failing pre-commit hook. The plan orders stop_and_wait first, hence architect. Fix: only wait for an existing proc to exit (or run the checkout and attribution checks before stopping), and do not mark a Suspended session Ended. Extend land_refuses_dirty_checkout_and_changes_nothing to assert !session_over and that a reply resumes.

The attribution check fails open on git log output it cannot parse. commits() splits records on 0x1e and silently drops any chunk whose first field is not a CommitId when no earlier commit has been parsed. With log.showSignature=true in the user or repo config, git log --format=... prints the signature verification text (Good git signature for ...) before each signed commit record; I measured this with an SSH-signed commit in a scratch repo. Every such chunk then fails CommitId::parse and is dropped, the list comes back empty, attribution_refusal finds nothing, commits_ahead is still >0, and a signed commit carrying Co-Authored-By: Claude merges. The owner config does not set this today, but the rule the function states for itself is that a commit that was not read cannot be cleared. Fix: pass --no-show-signature (and -c log.showSignature=false). Return an error for any unparseable chunk with no previous record, and refuse when list.len() != rev-list --count.

merge() ignores the result of git merge --abort and reports Conflict (nothing changed in the checkout) without checking that MERGE_HEAD is gone afterwards. If the abort fails (for example index.lock held by a background git run from an IDE), the owner checkout is left mid-merge with conflict markers while Orchestra says the branch and worktree were kept. Re-check MERGE_HEAD after the abort and return a distinct fixed error.

merge passes the bare name orchestra/<id>, but commits() and commits_ahead() read refs/heads/orchestra/<id>. Git resolves refs/<name> and refs/tags/<name> before refs/heads/<name>, so a tag named orchestra/t1 (which a task session could create, since refs are shared) would be merged instead of the checked branch. Merge refs/heads/<branch>, or the exact tip id that was checked.

discard_task on a Queued task is not atomic. begin_task sets busy and releases the lock, then update_task sets Discarded. claim_next ignores busy, so a pump in between can claim the task, and start_in then overwrites the status with Running: a discarded task runs. The window is microseconds. cancel_task does it under one lock; do the same here, or make claim_next skip busy tasks.

The Landed/Discarded outcome of a cleanup_pending task lives only in the free-text note, parsed with starts_with(Discarded). This is robust today: notes are Rust-built, the title never enters them, restore and sync never rewrite a cleanup_pending note, and an unrecognised note defaults to Landed and git branch -d, which never loses unmerged work. It is brittle to any future note change, though, and a Landed retry stays pending forever if the owner moves HEAD off the base before the retry (-d then reports not merged). A persisted outcome field (store.rs, outside s4) would be cleaner.

generated_with_claude matches generated with claude anywhere in a line, so prose such as docs generated with Claude help refuses the land. This fails closed and arguably counts as attribution anyway. The listed patterns (Co-Authored-By naming Claude or Anthropic, Claude-Session, Generated with [Claude Code], both links, noreply@anthropic.com as author or committer) are all detected case-insensitively on every commit in base..branch, including the leftover commit Orchestra makes and the merge message, and human co-authors pass. Nothing is read from graph_agents.

The attribution scan reads through replace refs. refs are shared with the task worktree, so a task session can run git replace <its commit> <clean commit>. I measured this in raw git with a marker message, because the commit guard rightly blocks writing a real trailer even in scratch. With the exact commits() argv, %H shows the original sha and %B shows the replacement's clean message. rev-list --count is 1 either way. git merge then records the original object, and git --no-replace-objects log shows the original message on the merged parent. A count check would not catch this. Only a deliberate session could do it, which is why this is a note. Fix: run commits() (and commits_ahead) as git --no-replace-objects, or set GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1.

Because the checks now run before the pause, the attribution scan happens before the child is killed. After the pause it runs again only if Orchestra stages leftovers. merge() merges refs/heads/<branch> as it stands at merge time, not the tip that was checked. A commit that lands on the branch between the first commits() and the kill is merged unchecked. The child of a Done task is idle and the job object kills its whole tree, so the window is tiny, but it is a regression from attempt 1's order. Fix: after pause_and_wait, re-run commits() and attribution_refusal unconditionally (cheap), or record the checked tip and merge that id.

A merge refused by a hook is reported as a conflict. Probe: a commit-msg hook that exits 1. git merge --no-ff -m m refs/heads/orchestra/t2 returns rc=1 and leaves MERGE_HEAD, so merge() aborts (correctly, nothing is left mid-merge) and returns Conflict. Land then sets the note 'conflicts, merge orchestra/<id> by hand' and says the merge has conflicts. That is safe but tells the owner the wrong reason. The new abort re-check is correct: MERGE_HEAD is read with unwrap_or(true), and a failed abort returns a distinct fixed error.

Checked and sound, recorded so the next reader can skip it. claim_next now skips busy tasks. discard is the only action begin_task allows on a Queued task, so FIFO and MAX_RUNNING_TASKS are unchanged, and begin_task still refuses a task that is starting. The s3 tests pass in the full run. merge uses refs/heads/<branch>, and branch -d/-D with the bare name is safe because git branch only names refs/heads. pause_and_wait bumps spawn_gen so the exit is ignored, frees a slot only if one was held, and leaves a Done task Done (task::sync maps Suspended+Done to Done, session_over false). resume_with refuses while the task is busy, so a reply cannot respawn a child into the worktree mid-land. Plain sessions, commands.rs and the IPC shapes are untouched. The note-encoded Landed/Discarded outcome and the prose false positive remain as attempt 1 described them.

findings.detail: Grafts still hide a commit from the scan. --no-replace-objects does not disable <common git dir>/info/grafts. I measured this in scratch with the exact commits() argv: base -> C1 (message with a Claude trailer) -> C2 (clean), plus a grafts line '<C2> <base>'. log shows only C2, rev-list --count is 1, so the count check passes and nothing is flagged. git merge --no-ff refs/heads/orchestra/t1 then succeeds. Once the grafts file is removed, the merged history contains C1 and its trailer. Only a session that sets out to do this can trigger it: it must write into the owner's .git, and such a session could just as well write refs or hooks. That makes it a note, the same severity attempt 2 gave replace refs. The commit message's claim covers only replace refs, and that claim is true. Fix, measured: set GIT_GRAFT_FILE in run() to a path that does not exist. rev-list --count then went from 1 to 2. A .git/shallow file cutting at the task tip does not hide anything: there is no merge base, and the merge fails with 'refusing to merge unrelated histories'.

Carried over from attempt 2, unchanged and not claimed as fixed: land checks commits() before pause_and_wait. After the pause it re-reads them only when Orchestra commits leftovers. merge() merges refs/heads/<branch> as it stands at merge time. A commit made between the first check and the kill merges unchecked. The window is tiny: the child of a Done task is idle, and the job object kills its whole tree. Re-run commits() unconditionally after the pause, or merge the tip id that was checked.

Side effects of applying GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS to every command: merge, commit, worktree add, diff and branch -d now see real objects in the owner's repo, and hooks run by merge or commit inherit the variable. On a repo with no replace refs (the normal case) nothing changes. On a repo where the owner uses replace refs on purpose, merge-base and the diff are computed on the real graph, not the view the owner sees. The result stays consistent: what the review shows is what lands, and the commit is valid history. I found no harmful effect.

Checked and sound. Over-count: a header forged in a message yields an extra parsed entry, and commits() returns 'could not read every task commit'. This is tested in commits_errors_when_a_forged_header_makes_the_count_differ and end to end in land_refuses_when_the_task_commits_cannot_be_read_and_stays_replyable, which also checks session_over=false, a working reply, unchanged HEAD and branch, and the worktree present. Under-count: I tried C2 messages ending in RS+junk, three FS, a trailing FS, and RS + 39 hex, each over a C1 that carried a trailer. Every case parsed 2 records and found the trailer. A real record cannot be absorbed, because splitting happens on git's own terminator and %H%x1f%ae%x1f%ce%x1f always emits three FS. A count/log race between the two git calls also fails closed. With log.showSignature=true and an SSH-signed commit, plain log puts the signature text first, while Orchestra's argv gives clean records. Each pattern form (Co-Authored-By, lowercase co-authored-by, Claude-Session, Generated with [Claude Code] plus link, claude.ai/code) survives into the parsed message, and a noreply@anthropic.com author lands in author_email. The detector cases are covered by attribution_detector_flags_each_pattern. The new tests fail without the new code: replace ref, count check, leading chunk.

Re-derived the limit: claim, the starting flag, start_in's Running flip and resume's check-plus-begin_resume-plus-sync all happen under one Inner lock, so the pump, a restore with paused tasks and follow-ups cannot exceed 2. cwd_of guards all three spawn sites; the generation bump on Idle retires the old child's late exit; kill and wait run off-lock. The builder's choices (cancel to discarded, abandoned paused resume to done, cfg(test) on_output) are sound. Notes: a plain session whose folder vanishes mid-run now ends instead of staying resumable; resume_with does not gate on task status.

findings.issue: Plain-session behaviour change. resume_with maps every CwdError::Project, including a project folder that vanished after load (is_dir false), to fail_resume, which leaves the session permanently Ended with an error item. Before (7e62e10 plus s2's spawn dir check), a vanished folder was a spawn error followed by abort_resume, so the session stayed Suspended and could be resumed once the folder came back. Example: the owner renames the project folder, replies, then renames it back. The session can no longer continue. The design only required refusing without spawning. Suggest abort_resume semantics (refuse, stay Suspended) for the is_dir case and fail_resume only when the project entry itself is gone.

resume_with checks the task limit but not the task's status. A task whose status sync leaves alone (Error, and later CleanupPending or Landing) is not counted by is_active, yet its suspended session can still be resumed whenever its worktree exists. In s3 this is reachable only from a state file with an unknown status ('frozen' loads as Error and keeps an in-base worktree), and that reply spawns claude outside MAX_RUNNING_TASKS. s4's busy flag covers landing, but cleanup_pending and error are not covered. Suggest refusing a task resume unless the status is Done or NeedsInput.

start_task stores the worktree and branch before start_in saves. A crash or kill in that window persists a Queued task that already has a worktree and an orchestra/tN branch. On relaunch the pump picks orchestra/tN-2, worktree_add then fails on the existing path, and the task goes to Error, leaving an orphan worktree and branch for manual cleanup. The window is narrow, so this is a note.

A pump already inside start_task when shutdown starts can still spawn: claim_next checks shutting_down, but start_in does not. The child is contained by the KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE job, and its state is not saved, so this is only a note.

Judged the builder's choices. (1) A paused (NeedsInput, Suspended) task whose resume spawn fails ends up Done, not paused: Running plus Suspended maps to Done. Both states can take a reply and neither counts toward the limit, so this is only cosmetic (the paused note is lost). (2) cancel to Discarded with the note 'Cancelled before it started' fits the closed enum. (3) on_output as cfg(test): every production sink goes through handle_output with a generation (0 for start, the bumped value for resume), so retired children are always filtered.
